newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia official slams Council of Europe.
newsitem.headline: Russia official slams Council of Europe.

text.p: A Russian Foreign ministry official on Thursday slammed a decision by the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe to suspend Belarus's special guest status, Interfax news agency said.

Interfax quoted foreign ministry spokesman Vladimir Andreyev as saying that the suspension, prompted by doubts over the legitimacy of the former Soviet republic's new parliament, was "hasty and inadequate".

The indefinite suspension was announced on Monday in the French city of Strasbourg by assembly president Leni Fischer, who said Belarus's new constitution, adopted by a controversial referendum in November, was illegal and fell short of minimum democratic standards.
Belarus remains the only European country outside former Yugoslavia yet to be admitted to the Council.
"An attempt to isolate the Belarussian parliament can hardly answer the spirit of the organisation, the task of building a new Europe, strengthening the unity of the continent," Andreyev said.

"A balanced analysis of Belarus developments, constructive dialogue and real assistance rather than ostracism from the Council of Europe would help the democratic development of Belarus society, its progress towards reforms," he added.
The leaders of Russia and Belarus, Boris Yeltsin and Alexander Lukashenko, have announced plans to move toward reunification of the Slav states.

Yeltsin, who is now in hospital recovering from pneumonia, said last week that Russia and Belarus should consider the idea of a possible referendum in both states over unification "in one form or another".
Yeltsin's liberal opponents accuse the Russian leader of turning a blind eye to human rights violations under the authoritarian Lukashenko, but the Kremlin rejects such charges.
